newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha weakens on softer Asian prices, crude.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha weakens on softer Asian prices, crude.

text.p: NWE naphtha weakened on Friday on easier crude, sluggish gasoline and a softening of prices in the dominant Asian market, traders said.
One player was heard offering April paper at $197 cif NWE, but was not believed to have received any bids close to that.

A German end-user offered 10,000 tonnes of Dow spec material at $196 cif NWE, but bids came nowhere near. "We really haven't received any respectable bids, of course we've seen the odd one around the $190 level," the player said.
On the swaps front, the curve went into contango with April talked around $201/$202 cif NWE and May at $202/$202.50.

Traders attributed part of the market's softening to weaker Asian prices as buyers remained elusive. Suggestions by Asian traders that many April requirements had been covered had also pressured the market.
Some traders speculated that the market was being pushed lower by players looking to move material East. "They want to keep the East-West spread wide," said one.
